title: Real lab: find and kill a runaway process
instruction: Real Linux box. A stray process is running the command `sleep 99999` and eating a slot you need. Find its PID (try `ps aux | grep sleep`) and kill it. Then click Verify.
setup: sleep 99999 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/.runaway; echo "(a stray 'sleep 99999' process is now running)"

verify.command: if kill -0 $(cat /tmp/.runaway 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null; then echo PROC_STILL_RUNNING; else echo PROC_GONE; fi
verify.success: Solved! You found a process and stopped it. ps/pgrep to find, kill (or pkill -f) to stop. Signals: kill sends TERM by default (polite); kill -9 sends KILL (forceful, last resort).
verify.fail: It's still running. Find the PID (ps aux | grep sleep, or pgrep -f 'sleep 99999') and kill it.

hint: pgrep -f 'sleep 99999'   to get the PID, then  kill <PID>     (or in one go: pkill -f 'sleep 99999')
